record.paper_title: Open Problems in the Topology of Manifolds
record.original_question: For knots, the stabilising number can be defined in both the topological category and the smooth category, with the smooth version requiring the bounding disks to be smoothly embedded. Is there a knot K with Arf invariant zero that is not topologically slice and satisfies 0 < sn_top(K) < sn_smooth(K), so that the topological and smooth stabilising numbers differ?

evidence.quote: Remark. The definition of the stabilising number also makes sense in the smooth category (one requires that the discs be smoothly embedded).

Question B. Is there a difference between the topological and smooth stabilising numbers of a knot? More precisely, is there a non-topological slice, Arf invariant zero knot K such that 0 < sntop(K) < snsmooth(K)?

artifact.self_contained_problem:
Background and definitions. Let K be an oriented knot in the 3-sphere S^3. For a non-negative integer n, write nS = (S^2 × S^2)^{# n} for the connected sum of n copies of S^2 × S^2. View S^3 as the boundary of the 4-ball B^4, and consider the boundary-connected sum B^4 ♮ nS, whose boundary is still S^3.

(a) The topological stabilising number sn_top(K) is defined to be the smallest non-negative integer n such that K bounds a locally flat, properly embedded disk in B^4 ♮ nS. If no such n exists, set sn_top(K) = ∞.

(b) The smooth stabilising number sn_smooth(K) is defined to be the smallest non-negative integer n such that K bounds a smoothly properly embedded disk in B^4 ♮ nS. If no such n exists, set sn_smooth(K) = ∞.

Clearly sn_top(K) ≤ sn_smooth(K). The Arf invariant Arf(K) ∈ Z/2 is the standard Z/2-valued concordance invariant; it is known that sn_top(K) and sn_smooth(K) are finite if and only if Arf(K) = 0. K is called topologically slice if sn_top(K) = 0.

Problem. Does there exist a knot K ⊂ S^3 with Arf(K) = 0 that is not topologically slice, and such that
    0 < sn_top(K) < sn_smooth(K)?
Equivalently, exhibit such a K or prove that for every non-topologically-slice knot K with Arf(K) = 0 one has sn_top(K) = sn_smooth(K).
artifact.status_search_result: Web searches reveal active research on stabilising/shake-slice numbers and on differences between smooth and topological 4-dimensional invariants of knots, including recent work on knots that are topologically but not smoothly n-shake slice. No source was found announcing a resolution of the specific question comparing sn_top and sn_smooth for non-topologically-slice knots of Arf invariant zero, so the problem appears to remain open.

status_evidence.title: Embedding spheres in knot traces
status_evidence.snippet: infinitely many knots that are n-shake slice but neither smoothly n-shake slice nor (topologically) slice
status_evidence.claim: Closely related smooth-vs-topological stabilisation problems are actively studied but the specific comparison sn_top<sn_smooth for Arf=0 non-slice knots is not announced as solved.

status_evidence.title: Deep and shallow slice knots in 4-manifolds
status_evidence.snippet: Slice knots in connected sums of S^2 x S^2 and related stabilisations
status_evidence.claim: Recent literature discusses sliceness after stabilisation in both categories without resolving the stated dichotomy.
